A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VERINA and its 189 Lean programming problems. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite renamed subsets, relocated analyses, and additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, contextual-input experiments, iterative proof-refinement results, and failure analyses in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds specialized-prover and agentic results, specification-evaluator validation, and manual inspection outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: The specification evaluator changes from testing alone to a hybrid procedure that first attempts an LLM-generated formal proof and falls back to testing when inconclusive (Section 4.1, Figure 3). This adds a substantive certification component; v1 explicitly deferred such proving capabilities.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 189 problems: 49 translated MBPP-DFY problems, 59 CloverBench problems, and 81 student submissions. VERINA-BASIC/ADV become VERINA-A/B, retaining the same coverage and generation tasks. The added CLEVER discussion does not constitute evaluation on another dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds Goedel Prover V2 32B and Copra to proof comparisons, and extends refinement/direct-generation comparisons to Goedel and the existing DeepSeek prover. DeepSeek's CodeGen, SpecGen, and contextual-comparison entries are removed. DeepSeek Prover 2 7B in v1 and DeepSeek Prover V2 7B in v2 use the same checkpoint.

E3.justification: Specification checking now attempts formal proofs before testing. Appendix A.3 revises DeepSeek ProofGen prompting from the shared template to its own template; the added Goedel model also uses its own template. New evaluation procedures include Copra with o4-mini and at most 64 queries, plus manual inspection of 20 randomly selected proof/testing disagreements.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 and Table 5 add a direct investigation of specification-evaluator reliability, comparing two provers against testing and manually checking disagreements. The refinement-versus-direct-generation analysis gains specialized provers. Existing difficulty comparisons and Appendix C case studies are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report five sampled responses per model/problem for pass@1 estimation, bounds arising from unknown specification evaluations, and the same property-testing seed of 42. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting practices are introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 8 updates retained specification-guided CodeGen scores, including o4-mini from 63.8% to 65.9%. New proof results include Goedel at 11.2% and Copra at 7.9% with up to 64 queries. DeepSeek's 0.0% result is replaced by 11.1% under revised prompting, preventing a same-setting gain interpretation. Table 5 adds certification rates of 1.6–3.7%, testing totals of 51.0% and 41.6%, and accompanying successful manual checks. DeepSeek CodeGen/SpecGen results are removed.

T1.justification: The four formal soundness/completeness implications and their reductions to positive/negative test checks are retained in Section 4.1 and the implementation appendix. Appendix C's proof examples are also retained. The new proof-success measurements introduce empirical evidence rather than new theoretical derivations.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a manually curated, compositional benchmark for three generation tasks. v2 recasts specification evaluation as combining formal proving and testing, and narrows the introduction's best-model claim to general-purpose LLMs while acknowledging stronger specialized proof models.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds the interpretation that o4-mini remains competitive on difficult instances despite specialized provers' overall advantages. v2 removes v1's explicit warning about definitionally equivalent code/specification shortcuts and its disclosure that equivalence checks are unimplemented. The independent-generation workflow and principal dataset limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table 3 adds Goedel's checkpoint and hosting information, and the text documents specialized prompting and Copra's configuration. A new reproducibility statement reports supplementary code, data, and setup instructions. Public access URLs remain unchanged, while Appendix A.1 changes the licensing statement from current to prospective.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused comparison with concurrent CLEVER in Section 4.2 and Appendix A.4/Table 4, including task coverage and criticism of its ground-truth requirement. It adds specialized-prover, Copra, and Lean/Rust references and removes the Lean-SMT and BEq discussions. The existing related-work taxonomy remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. v2 revises the evaluator and experimental narrative, renames the subsets, moves difficulty discussion into Appendix B, changes citation style, and adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. These are focused edits and reorganizations rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 3, adds the proof-comparison Figure 6 and Tables 4–5, relocates the difficulty chart, and expands and redisplays refinement plots across Figure 7 and Appendix Figure 14. It also changes legends, table membership, prompt/code formatting, and the document's overall page template.

improvement.justification: The new evaluator validation, 20-case manual audit, and specialized/agentic proof comparisons strengthen empirical support beyond v1. The gain is limited: validation remains narrow, and Appendix A.4 criticizes CLEVER's ground-truth requirement without reconciling VERINA's own reliance on ground-truth specifications in Section 4.1. The added evidence improves the paper despite this positioning weakness.
